name: Proxmox_VE_Node_Subscription
description: This Proxmox VE node's subscription status and renewal date, whether it needs a reboot to run its newest installed kernel, and how many of its Proxmox packages have an update waiting.
technicalNotes:
Script, two calls to this node per interval: /nodes/{node}/subscription and /nodes/{node}/apt/versions. The node is asked directly, at this resource's own hostname, and never through another node: another node would answer for itself. The subscription needs no privilege beyond authentication; the package versions need Sys.Audit on /nodes/{node}, which PVEAuditor includes. If that read fails, RebootRequired and UpdatesAvailable read No Data and the subscription figures still report.

RebootRequired is 1 when the newest installed kernel package (proxmox-kernel-<version>-pve-signed, or the older pve-kernel-) is newer than the running kernel: the node was upgraded and not restarted. It raises a warning on the first poll that sees it. The API does not show a kernel pinned with proxmox-boot-tool kernel pin, so a node pinned to an older kernel reads 1; disable the alert on that node. A running kernel that is not a Proxmox build reads No Data.

UpdatesAvailable counts the Proxmox packages (about 60, not every package on the node) whose version in the node's package cache is newer than the one installed. The node refreshes that cache itself, daily by default. It ships without a threshold. A node whose package cache knows no repository (proxmox-ve reports origin unknown) reads No Data rather than 0.

nextduedate is a YYYY-MM-DD string rather than an epoch, so it is parsed as UTC midnight. A node with no subscription has no due date at all and reports none -- zero days remaining would read as 'expires today' on every unlicensed node.

Active ships without a threshold: an unsubscribed node is a licensing fact, not a fault, and a homelab would alert forever. Set a threshold where a subscription is genuinely expected.

Applies on ProxmoxVE_Node resources the NetScan has not marked unreachable (pve.netscan.reachable). The suite has no addCategory_* PropertySource: the NetScan sets the categories and pve.cluster.role, and the product page lists them for a resource added by hand.

datapoints.name: Active
datapoints.description: 1 when the node reports an active subscription. Ships without a threshold: an unsubscribed node is a licensing fact, not a fault.

datapoints.name: Sockets
datapoints.description: CPU sockets the subscription key covers.

datapoints.name: DaysUntilDue
datapoints.description: Days until the subscription's next due date. Withheld on a node with no subscription rather than reported as zero.
datapoints.alertBody: The Proxmox subscription on node ##INSTANCE## is due in ##VALUE## days. If it lapses, the node loses access to the enterprise repository and its updates.

datapoints.name: RebootRequired
datapoints.description: 1 when the newest installed kernel is newer than the running one, so the node needs a reboot to finish its upgrade. No Data when the package versions cannot be read.
datapoints.alertBody:
Proxmox node ##HOSTNAME## has a newer kernel installed than the one it is running, so it was upgraded and has not been restarted. Its security and bug fixes are not in effect until it reboots. Migrate its guests and reboot it in a maintenance window. If the node is pinned to an older kernel on purpose (proxmox-boot-tool kernel pin), disable this alert on it.

Status: ##ALERTVALUEDISPLAYSTATUSNAME## (##VALUE##).

This started at ##START##, ##DURATION## ago.

datapoints.name: UpdatesAvailable
datapoints.description: Proxmox packages on the node with a newer version in its package cache. Ships without a threshold. No Data when the cache knows no repository.

datapoints.name: DaysSinceLastCheck
datapoints.description: Days since Proxmox last validated the key against the subscription server.
